account:
Today seems mostly routine so far. I read my appointments, attended morning office hours, and walked the plaza market at ten. The secretary had no correspondence or confirmed news and initially could not identify the cottage for afternoon tea. I have now spoken directly with the neighbour, who confirmed that tea is at three at the east-bank cottage, road point (16, -60, 105). I have just reached home for noon lunch, with town accounts scheduled in the office at one.

The main recurring market news concerns the baker. Several townspeople reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery; later, Townsfolk 30 reported a sack of bread at the inn, and Townsfolk 10 reported one at the market. I personally saw the baker put bread into the bakery-stall chest at 10:50. These observations suggest baking, restocking, and perhaps deliveries, but I have no evidence of anything improper or exceptional.

One small change caught my attention: at 10:53 a lantern appeared at (-58, -60, 31), near the town hall's great-hall tables. Later I saw the builder walking through town holding a lantern. This might be ordinary lighting work, but I did not see who placed the lantern or hear why it was put there, so I cannot connect it confidently to the builder or any event. No one has yet brought a definite concern to my attention.
